basis: Actual view_image(detail=original) of 12 five-column comparison pages, each with az=-60, az=120, fixed front section and fixed side section; six supplementary single-cell pages were actually viewed. Labels and observations below were individually authored from images only. No metrics, source-parent reconstruction ranking, or FINAL images were used.
semantics: Body is independent of C adoption. Side-panel, pedestal and leg support designs can all be reasonable. NOT_CLEAR is not certified absence. Slat spacing, hollow supports and finite-section endpoints are not automatically visible fragmentation. An upper/lower surface mismatch informs adoption but alone does not establish folding. UNCERTAIN is retained when visible evidence does not resolve C use or fine debris.
metadata_assembly: Only flattening the 60 explicitly authored manual rows and attaching verified image hashes/IDs; no label heuristic or score-derived rating.

records.observation: Both oblique views show a long box/trough-like body with high gray walls around a much less exposed blue surface. A narrow diagonal opening is visible in the long gray face. The fixed sections place C inside the wall height rather than on an obvious usable top. The walls provide visible support, but the intended seating role remains uncertain after viewing the single-cell page.

A faceted gray slab spans two broad pedestal-like supports in both oblique views. The blue C projects below and beside that slab. Front and side sections show the gray seating block substantially above C, so the generated bench is recognizable while C is not its seating surface. No clear loose fragment or folded panel is resolved.

The gray rounded/faceted top and two broad lower supports form a recognizable bench. Blue C lies through the lower part of the structure and protrudes at the side. Both sections separate its level from the gray top. Minor facet changes do not provide clear visible evidence of debris or folding.
